subject: Re: Measurement & Billing clause update (metering language) — review + approval
related_links: Linear: PM-614 (Coordinate legal review of ‘measurement and billing’ language updates)
Jira: SUP-3112 (Invoice tokens higher than console by ~6%)
body:
From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 14, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Measurement & Billing clause update (metering language) — review requested

Michael —

Per PM-614, attaching proposed updates to the MSA “Measurement & Billing” clause (Section 4.3) to align with current metering behavior and the Finance/Telemetry sanity checks program.

Key goals (non-negotiables from Finance):
- Define “Usage” broadly enough to cover tokens/embedding units/rerank units/requests + future meters.
- Clarify measurement source of truth (our systems) while staying reasonable.
- Add a dispute window (proposal: 30 days from invoice) and process for good-faith review.
- Address retries/failed requests/streaming disconnects (we should not over-promise).

Please review for risk exposure + any redlines. We have a customer procurement thread that is explicitly asking for clarity on measurement and audit rights (Evergreen Health Systems).

Attachments:
- Redwood_MSA_Clause_4.3_Measurement_and_Billing_v5_REDLINE.docx
- Redwood_MSA_Clause_4.3_Measurement_and_Billing_v5_CLEAN.docx
- Metering_Definitions_Appendix_A_v3.pdf (optional appendix if we want to reference “Usage Units” definitions)

Thanks,
Sofia Mendes
Commercial Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 14, 2026 at 11:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Measurement & Billing clause update (metering language) — review requested

Reviewed. This is directionally fine, but I want to tighten a few items before we call this “approved.” Notes below.

1) “Our measurement is final” language
- Current draft says: “Redwood’s measurement systems will be the system of record for billing.”
- Fine, but avoid “final and binding” unless we also expressly provide a dispute mechanism. Otherwise it reads one-sided and creates procurement friction.

2) Dispute window
- 30 days is reasonable. Add: disputes must include “reasonably sufficient detail” (invoice number, time window, request IDs if available) and customer must pay undisputed amounts on time.
- Clarify that failure to dispute within the window is a waiver.

3) Audit rights
- Don’t introduce new audit rights here. The draft appendix language implies a right to “audit billing records.” That belongs (if anywhere) in the general audit clause and we should keep it limited.
- If Evergreen is pushing: we can offer a narrow “review” process (we’ll provide relevant logs/exports), not an on-prem “audit.”

4) Streaming / partial completions
- Avoid promising we never charge for partial output. Better: bill for “Usage recorded up to termination” (client disconnect, timeouts).
- Also explicitly exclude outages where we returned an error before output began (no billable completion tokens, etc.). Keep it high-level.

5) Retries
- We should not say “retries are never billed.” Sometimes customers configure retries client-side and we may not distinguish intent.
- Safer: “Usage associated with requests processed by the Services, including customer-initiated retries” is billable; but we may credit in case of a confirmed service defect.

Sofia — if you want, I can mark up a proposed “final” paragraph-level version to reduce iteration.

Michael Grant
General Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 14, 2026 at 12:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Measurement & Billing clause update (metering language) — review requested

+1 to Michael’s point on retries. We have at least one recent ticket (SUP-3112) where “double counting” was actually confusion around client retries vs server retries.

From Finance perspective, we need:
- “pay undisputed amounts” language
- dispute window
- permission to correct errors (credits on a forward invoice rather than reopening closed periods)

Emily can add a short operational note (how we’ll provide evidence: invoice_run_id, usage export, etc.) but I’d prefer we keep contract language principle-based.

Laura

From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 8:17 AM PST
Subject: Re: Measurement & Billing clause update (metering language) — review requested

Thanks. I agree with all five points.

I’ll revise to:
- remove “final and binding” tone and add explicit dispute procedure
- add waiver + “reasonably sufficient detail” + pay undisputed amounts
- remove any hint of customer audit right; keep “review + supporting records” only
- update streaming language to “recorded up to termination”
- update retries language to include customer-initiated retries as billable; retain ability to credit for service defects

Michael — if you can send your paragraph-level “final” wording for Section 4.3, that would help me land this quickly.

Also: Evergreen’s counsel (Northbridge Legal; Avery Chen) asked yesterday if we can reference our public docs for meter definitions. I think we can say “as described in the Order Form or Documentation” but avoid making docs controlling if they change.

Sofia

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 10:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: Measurement & Billing clause update (metering language) — proposed final wording

Here’s proposed “final” language for Section 4.3 (Measurement and Billing). Use/adapt as needed.

----
4.3 Measurement and Billing.
(a) Usage Measurement. Fees for the Services may be based on usage (“Usage”). Usage may include, without limitation, tokens processed, requests, embeddings units, reranking units, compute time, throughput reservations, or other consumption metrics described in an Order Form or the Documentation (“Usage Units”). Redwood will measure Usage using its systems and logs, which are intended to accurately record and aggregate Usage Units.

(b) Invoicing. Redwood will invoice Customer in accordance with the applicable Order Form. Usage is calculated based on Usage recorded during the applicable billing period. For streamed or otherwise incremental responses, Usage may be recorded up to the time the response is completed or terminated (including due to Customer disconnects, timeouts, or similar events). Usage associated with requests processed by the Services, including Customer-initiated retries, is billable, unless otherwise expressly stated in an Order Form.

(c) Disputes. Customer must notify Redwood in writing of any good-faith dispute regarding an invoice within thirty (30) days of the invoice date and provide reasonably sufficient detail to allow Redwood to investigate (including invoice number, relevant date range, and, if available, request identifiers or usage exports). Customer will timely pay all undisputed amounts. If the Parties determine that an invoice contains an error, Redwood will correct the error by issuing a credit on a future invoice or otherwise adjusting charges as agreed.

(d) Records. Upon request, Redwood will provide reasonable supporting information regarding the measured Usage underlying an invoice, subject to Redwood’s confidentiality and security obligations.
----

Two drafting notes:
- I kept docs as descriptive but not controlling. If Order Form conflicts, Order Form should control.
- I avoided “sole discretion”/“final determination.” This reads more balanced and is easier in procurement.

Michael

From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Avery Chen <avery.chen@northbridgelegal.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 15, 2026 at 3:09 PM PST
Subject: Evergreen / Redwood MSA — updated Measurement & Billing language

Avery —

Following up on your question re: how Redwood measures usage and how billing disputes are handled.

We’ve updated our standard “Measurement and Billing” section to:
- define the types of usage units that may apply (tokens, embedding units, reranking units, requests, reserved capacity metrics)
- clarify how streaming/partial completions are measured (usage recorded up to termination)
- provide a 30-day invoice dispute window and a process for providing supporting information

We can also provide a short appendix describing current usage units at a high level (non-exhaustive), but note that the applicable Order Form will specify the usage units that apply to your subscription.

If helpful, I can send the clean clause text for your review.

Best,
Sofia Mendes
Commercial Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: Avery Chen <avery.chen@northbridgelegal.com>
To: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 16, 2026 at 9:32 AM PST
Subject: Re: Evergreen / Redwood MSA — updated Measurement & Billing language

Sofia,

Thanks. Please send the clean clause text.

Two things we’ll be looking for:
1) A commitment that if Evergreen disputes in good faith, Redwood will provide reasonable backup (not just “at Redwood’s discretion”).
2) Clarity that usage resulting from Redwood service defects will not be charged (e.g., failed requests, disconnect-related artifacts).

Separately, our standard is a 60-day invoice dispute window, but we can discuss.

Regards,
Avery Chen
Northbridge Legal
Counsel to Evergreen Health Systems

From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 16, 2026 at 11:06 AM PST
Subject: Re: Measurement & Billing clause update (metering language) — Evergreen feedback

FYI from Evergreen counsel:
- wants a firmer commitment we’ll provide backup (I think we already do)
- wants a statement that service-defect usage isn’t charged (this is the tricky one)
- asked for 60-day dispute window

Michael — are you comfortable holding the line at 30 days? Finance prefers 30 for close discipline, but we may need a negotiation position.

On service defects: I’m hesitant to say “not charged” broadly. Can we instead say we’ll correct errors if we confirm a billing error or service defect that materially impacted measurement?

Sofia


---

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Jan 16, 2026 at 1:22 PM PST
Subject: Re: Measurement & Billing clause update (metering language) — Evergreen feedback

Agree: do NOT promise “service defects not charged” in a blanket way. It creates ambiguity (what’s a defect vs customer integration) and encourages disputes.

Suggested compromise language for counsel:
- Keep clause as drafted.
- Add one sentence in disputes subsection: “If Redwood confirms a billing error or a Service defect that materially affected Usage measurement, Redwood will correct the affected charges.”

On dispute window:
- Default stays 30 days. Negotiation fallback for strategic enterprise: up to 45 days.
- 60 days is too long given monthly invoicing cadence + close.

If Evergreen is pushing hard, we can deal-paper it in their Order Form (not change standard MSA).

Michael


---

From: Sofia Mendes <sofia.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Stone <emily.stone@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Jan 17, 2026 at 4:38 PM PST
Subject: Measurement & Billing clause — final approved (v6)

All —

I incorporated Michael’s proposed text + added the single sentence re: confirmed billing error/service defect materially affecting measurement.

Final (v6) position:
- Standard MSA: 30-day dispute window
- Negotiation fallback (deal-paper only): up to 45 days if needed
- No audit right added; we provide reasonable supporting info

Michael — please reply “approved” so I can mark PM-614 as complete and update the template packet.

Also attaching the updated clean clause text (v6) and a short appendix PDF we can share if requested.

Attachments:
- Redwood_MSA_Clause_4.3_Measurement_and_Billing_v5_CLEAN.docx (updated to v6 content)
- Metering_Definitions_Appendix_A_v3.pdf

Sofia
